FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
challenging the judgment and award dated 16.11.2018 in MVC No.1441/2017, passed by the IV NC:
2024:KHC:22249 Additional District and Sessions Judge, Hassan District (sitting at Channarayapatna).

sentences.text:
Regional Manager vs Smt. Puppamma on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91705429/
2 2.

The claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, seeking just and proper compensation on account of the death of Sri. Ayyappa, who succumbed to injuries sustained in a road accident on 06.07.2017.
The Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,36,000/- with interest at 9% per annum.
The Insurance Company is in appeal before this Court challenging the quantum of compensation.
3. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company.
4. It is noted that the death of Sri.Ayyappa in the road traffic accident on 06.07.2017 is not disputed.

As on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 63 years, and in the absence of proof of income, the notional income must be assessed at Rs.6,000/- per month according to the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for accidents occurred in the year 2017.
The Tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.3,36,000/- towards loss of dependency.

The Tribunal has committed an error by awarding compensation twice under the head 'loss of estate' for a sum of Rs.90,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively and also awarded Rs.3,00,000/- towards love and affection of petitioners 2 to 7, which is incorrect.
5. Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is re
- assessed as follows:

NC: 2024:KHC:22249 Heads Amount Sl. (In Rupees) No.
1.
Towards loss of Dependency 3,36,000 2.

Towards loss of Consortium(1st 40,000 petitioner)
3.
Towards loss of Estate 15,000 4.
Towards Funeral expenses 15,000 5.
Towards loss of filial consortium 2,40,000 of petitioners 2 to 7
6. In the result, the appeal is allowed-in-part.
The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
The claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.6,46,000/- as opposed to Rs.10,36,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. The compensation amount of Rs.6,46,000/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6%
per annum as against 9% awarded by the Tribunal.

8. The statutory amount in deposit as well as 50% of the amount deposited by the Insurance Company to be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.
